item: Pastor and leader (pastor_leader) — Futures Daily Word
angle: Behavioural design: the unit of reading, the trigger, the reward, the grace, the identity language, the return visit — for a person whose whole week is already full of other people's Bible reading.
thesis: A pastor does not need help doing the work. He needs the app to protect the ten minutes that produce nothing. The research says ~70% of SBC pastors already spend 8+ hours a week on sermon prep, 65% report loneliness (up from 42% in 2015) and 38% considered quitting in the past year (research, Persona 5). The behaviour at risk is not prep; it is the reading that is not for anyone else. So the design makes the personal reading the immediate, zero-decision move and puts every work surface one deliberate tap behind it — and then gives the work a real reward loop, because a pastor who reads with a pen in hand ends the week with Sunday already started. Right now the app does the opposite: the Preach card sits above the reading (HomeScreen.tsx:2106 vs the hero at 2138) and leaves the PWA entirely (PREP_URL, line 74). The identity line the app already writes — "This is your time — not ministry, just you and God" (persona-config.ts) — is the best sentence in the pastor path and the layout contradicts it before he scrolls.
principles: Personal first, work second. The reading and Between You & God own the screen; every prep surface is one tap below it. This restores Ashley's own 2 Sep ruling (Sermon Notes row demoted below the reading for pastor_leader) that PR #97 reversed.

Richer and clearer, never stripped. Nothing is deleted. Cards that arrive open and heavy arrive closed and named, keeping their full typography and the locked look when opened (ivory canvas, terracotta accent, white paper-mode reading panel, Georgia serif).

Never show a pastor a number the app made up. The Sunday card's "days this week" is currently Math.min(streak, 7) (HomeScreen.tsx:117) — a fabrication. Campus Overview already refuses to fabricate; the habit surfaces must match that standard or the whole trust panel is theatre.

The AI finds and organises; the pastor writes. 79% of pastors worry AI could replace God's role, 63% pastoral leadership, 71% are cautious (research, Persona 5). Every AI surface names its role and its sources on the same screen.

Reward the behaviour we want, not speed. The celebration is "Sunday is not blank", attached to filing verses while reading — not "minutes saved", which would import the productivity framing that kills the protected ten minutes.

Grace without accounting. No streak number until it is worth something, a real freeze already exists in streak.ts, and a return after a gap is greeted with "nothing to make up" — guilt-framed streak nudges drive notification opt-out and uninstall (research, cross-cutting 6).
Comfort is reachable from the pastor path without changing his path. Crisis is not a persona a pastor picks on a good day (research, Persona 6).

journey.day0: He arrives at pastor_leader through one of the four ChoosePathSheet doors; tapping the card saves with a real source and navigates Home (commit(next), ruling). PathArrivalStrip names the path once and shows sign-in state. The arrival seed opens today's reading credit-free, bypassing handleRead (ruling). If he has no plan, PastorStudyOnboarding renders below the reading in the plan_scripture gate; if he never answers it, PASTOR_CHAPTERS keeps the hero full (src/data/pastor.ts) so Day 0 requires zero decisions. Nothing asks him to prep. The only new thing on Day 0 is one quiet line under Between You & God: "Tap and hold any verse to file it for Sunday."
journey.first_session: Greeting uses the identity line, not a count. Reading is already open on the plate with audio. Directly under it, Between You & God with one of the fifteen leadership prompts and two buttons. Then, closed: Study this passage. Then For your message with its new subline. Then the plan cards, then the chapters, then Campus Overview, then Preach — which now sits below the reading and says out loud that it leaves Daily Word. Mark as read credits the day and writes the new dw_read_days ledger. Push is asked only after that first completed reading (already evidence-timed in App.tsx) and never inside the reading.
journey.return_visit: Same shape, no re-onboarding — PastorStudyOnboarding self-dismisses once any plan exists. Greeting bands on real read-days, not opens. From day 3 or 4 the This week's prep card appears above the fold-line of the second screen, because by then he has filed something; if he has filed nothing it does not render and the quiet filing hint stays for the first seven days only, then goes.
journey.week2: The prep bag has material, so three things change without any new prompt: the prep card shows a count and the preaching focus, the outline prompt in Bible AI has his own filed verses to shape, and the Sunday card has a real second tile. This is the compounding loop — read, file, Sunday is easier, read again. Sources become visible in the study card the first time he opens it, so by week 2 he has seen which commentary is public-domain and which line is AI.
journey.missed_day: streak.ts already bridges one missed day with a freeze replenished after 7 days (streak.ts:65-66) — keep it, untouched. Two or more days away resets the count, and that is where the copy matters: the greeting reads "You're back. Nothing to make up." No red, no lost-progress language, no catch-up plan, no make-up reading. The push after a gap names the chapter, never the streak.
journey.seasonal: The pastor's calendar moment is not Easter, it is Sunday, every week, forever, plus whatever series he is preaching. dw_sermon_prep_focus already holds the series. Use it: the hero eyebrow reads PREACHING · {focus} when a focus is set and PASTOR STUDY when it is not, and the Sunday card leads with the focus. Church-wide seasonal reads (research, cross-cutting 5) reach the pastor as a campus lever he sets for others, not as a nudge aimed at him.

comfort_access: One shared, path-neutral comfort door, reachable for a pastor without changing his saved path. It appears as a single quiet line at the foot of Between you and God — "If today is hard, open comfort" — and opens the comfort chapter as a full-screen sub-view over Home using useSubView alone, never useSubView plus useModalA11y (ruling: nested focus traps break keyboard and Android back). Inside it: one passage, slow audio first, low stimulus, the comfortMode toolbar restricted to Note and Close only, no streak, no count, no "complete", and no "Feeling Stronger?" graduation prompt, ever. It must never call saveSetup — his path stays pastor_leader, nothing is stamped, nothing syncs a persona change. This matters more for this persona than any other: 38% of pastors considered quitting in the past year and 65% report loneliness (research, Persona 5), and crisis is not something anyone selects from a menu on a good day (research, Persona 6). Paired with it, the safety flow: crisis language typed into Bible AI or a prayer request triggers a gentle confirm, then the region-correct line (988 in the US, 13 11 14 in Australia, 0800 543 354 in New Zealand) and a first-use disclosure that this is scripture and a church, not counselling — 81% of mental-health apps carry a liability disclaimer instead of a crisis resource and only 35% show one in-app, some with the wrong country's number (research, Persona 6, Crisis 2021). Which lines per congregation, and who at each campus receives a pastor's own prayer request, are Ashley's calls.
reminders: One push a day, no more, timed to when he actually opens rather than a number he guessed at setup — Duolingo's behaviour-inferred timing, which the research names as the pattern to copy (cross-cutting 6). The new dw_read_days ledger stores the local date and hour of each real completion for the last 14 days; after 5–7 sessions the reminder hour picker in More defaults to his modal hour and the card says so in one line. Copy is neutral and names the chapter, never the streak: "Today's chapter is open. This one is just for you." After a missed day the message acknowledges the gap and offers today, with no accounting: "Yesterday got away. Today's chapter is open." Guilt-framed streak reminders drive notification opt-out and uninstall, and that is a permanent loss of the only channel we have. Three live constraints hold: the ask fires only after the first completed reading and never stacks with PathAskedOnce (App.tsx gating, keep it); templates live hardcoded in netlify/functions/push-send.js with EN and ID only, so es/pt must be added there or Futuros pastors keep getting English; and pushSupported() allowlists futuresdailyword.com, www and localhost only, so none of this is verifiable on a deploy preview — verify on prod or localhost. The grace side stays in streak.ts exactly as it is: one freeze, replenished after 7 days, count bridged rather than reset. No new freeze rules.
instrumentation: pastor_read_done — a pastor completed the personal reading. Detail: read-days in the last 7, whether a plan or the PASTOR_CHAPTERS fallback served it. This is the D1/D7/D30 numerator for this path and the research says no public source will ever supply it.
pastor_prep_file — a verse was filed to the prep bag from the reading. Detail: ref. Proves the reward loop's trigger fires while reading, not in a separate work session.

pastor_prep_card_view / pastor_prep_handoff — the This week's prep card was seen, and its items were sent to Prep or to the outline prompt. Proves the filed pile is worth making visible; if handoff never fires, the card is decoration.

pastor_preach_exit — the Preach card was tapped. Detail: its screen position (above/below the reading) and the session's elapsed time before the tap. This is the single measurement that settles the demotion: if exits hold steady but pastor_read_done rises, the move worked.
pastor_study_open — Study this passage was expanded. Detail: which surface (commentary, greek, crossrefs, sources). If this collapses to near zero, the closed default is wrong and it goes back.
pastor_source_open — the source-and-licence footer or the sources list was opened. Directly tests the research's trust-panel claim.

pastor_ai_prompt — one of the four quick prompts fired. Detail: kind, whether a selection existed, whether the prep bag had items. trackBehavior already fires client-side as 'pastor:{kind}'; it needs a server-side allowlist entry to survive.

pastor_ai_subline_cohort — the framing A/B: 'For your message' alone versus with the 'It finds and organises' subline, measured on prompt-tap rate and on 7-day return. The research calls this the highest-leverage copy change for this persona; it is worthless untested.
pastor_sunday_card — shown, dismissed, or answered. Detail: read-days and filed count at the time. Tells us whether the Sunday beat is real.
pastor_comfort_open — comfort opened from the pastor path, with no persona change. Detail: entry point. Duty-of-care reach, and it must be reported separately from comfort-persona usage.
pastor_streak_repair — a freeze was spent. Detail: gap length. Proves grace is being used rather than people quietly leaving.
pastor_reminder_set / pastor_reminder_off — hour chosen, and every opt-out. Opt-out rate is the guard-rail metric on all reminder copy.

Path attached to the existing events: daily_reading, app_open and page_view must carry the persona in their detail, or D1/D7/D30 cannot be cut by path at all — which is the research's number-one build.

One dw_events table and one nightly rollup by path and cohort week. Everything above is unreadable without it, and TRACKED_EVENTS in src/utils/analytics.ts:24-31 is a hardcoded allowlist that silently drops anything not listed.
self_serve_levers: Already self-serve, keep: the preaching focus (dw_sermon_prep_focus — set in the wizard's step 13 or edited on the prep card), the campus code and campus (provisioned by pastor sign-in through my-campus-code, never typed by the client), the reminder hour and push on/off in More, the language switch, and the path itself through the swatch pill in the Home header.

NEW, zero backend: Write your own prompts. A pastor adds his own Between you and God prompts; his list rotates first and the bundled fifteen sit behind it. Stored as a personal dw_ key on the misc bag, fill-only, never campus-shared. This converts the single most hardcoded pastor content bank (persona-config.ts:473-487) into something he owns, and costs one small component.
NEW, zero backend: his own Sunday question. Same store, same rotation rule, replaces the bank on his device only.

NEW, intake-backed and campus-scoped: Campus reading. A campus pastor sets this week's passage for his campus; it replaces the PASTOR_CHAPTERS rotation as the hero fallback for readers at that campus. It goes through the existing intake pattern — format_preview, explicit confirm, submit — additive-only, campus-scoped, and every mint logged, exactly like the campus corner. If it ships as a /books/*.json asset it must be network-first with cache as offline fallback only, and CACHE_NAME, STATIC_CACHE and SW_VERSION all bump together, or returning readers never see the edit.

Still needs a developer, and should be named honestly rather than pretended away: PASTOR_CHAPTERS itself (src/data/pastor.ts), the wizard's plan mappings (PastorStudyOnboarding.tsx:147-256), the push templates and verse rotation (netlify/functions/push-send.js), the plan catalogue — where a plan id is referenced in four places and all four must be rewired or the wizard starts a dead plan — and the PREP_URL constant (HomeScreen.tsx:74). None of these has an admin surface today and none should be faked as one.

evidence.move: Identity language before counting; "You're back. Nothing to make up."
evidence.source: Research, cross-cutting 6: "Streaks work until they shame. Guilt-framed streak reminders drive notification opt-out and uninstall… streak repair rather than a hard reset." The app's own best line already exists: "This is your time — not ministry, just you and God" (persona-config.ts).

evidence.move: Behaviour-inferred reminder hour, one a day.

evidence.move: The Sunday beat rather than a seasonal campaign.
evidence.source: Research, cross-cutting 5: calendar moments drive the spikes; time-boxed shared events beat steady nudges. For a pastor the recurring calendar moment is Sunday. The pastor-only weekly review already exists and Ashley explicitly rejected widening it (project_daily_word_deep_dive_aug2026, Owner decision 8).

evidence.move: One-tap comfort from the pastor path without switching path.
evidence.source: Research, Persona 6 and "What to build first" item 2: "From every path: a persistent one-tap 'I need comfort now' that opens comfort without switching the saved path. Crisis is not a persona someone chooses on a good day."

open_decisions: The Preach card moving below the reading. It restores your own 2 Sep demotion ruling, but PR #97 deliberately put it back under the greeting as "always visible" — so one of the two was a mistake and only you know which. Everything else in this design assumes the reading comes first.

Commentary arriving closed for pastors behind "Study this passage". Nothing is removed and the open state is identical, but it changes what a pastor sees on arrival, so it is the item most likely to read as "stripped" on the preview link.

Whether 4D and H.E.A.T. appear inside the app as outline shapes on the AI prompt. They are the only two frameworks on record; putting them in the product is a decision about your own material, not a design question.

The crisis lines per congregation (988 US, 13 11 14 AU, 0800 543 354 NZ are drafted) and who at each campus receives a pastor's own prayer request — including whether a pastor's request routes to a peer rather than to his own campus.
Whether a campus pastor may set a campus reading through intake, or whether the reading stays central and campuses only get the campus corner.
Whether pastor push copy differs from congregation copy, and whether Spanish and Portuguese push templates are commissioned now — today a Futuros pastor gets an English notification.
Whether the pastor tier is priced flat, and at what (the research flags the Logos subscription backlash; nothing in this design depends on the answer).
risks: Moving the Preach card below the reading will reduce taps on it. That is the point, but if Pastors Sermon Prep sessions fall without pastor_read_done rising, the trade failed — pastor_preach_exit with its position in the detail is the instrument that settles it, and the move is one line to revert.

The closed commentary default is the one change that could read as "completely stripped" again. Mitigate by shipping it on the preview link with both states visible and the card's full typography intact when open, and by naming that nothing was deleted.

dw_read_days is a new synced key. It must merge into what is currently in localStorage and touch only its own field — never be rebuilt from React state, which once destroyed nine days of a reader's progress across devices — and it rides the misc bag fill-only with pushNow on write.
Adding a prep_bag key to pastor_leader's sectionOrder touches persona-config.ts, which is pinned by tests for the other four personas; the diff must show no other persona's sectionOrder moving.

Extending TRACKED_EVENTS requires the server aggregate to tolerate event types it does not know, or new events are silently dropped and the whole instrumentation build reads as working while recording nothing.

The campus-reading lever inherits a known, accepted exposure: any @futures.church mailbox can self-assign a campus on its first /staff submission and then obtain that campus's code. It adds no new power over the campus corner, but it must stay campus-scoped, additive-only and logged.
Push copy and templates live in a Netlify function with no CMS, so every wording change is a deploy — and none of it is verifiable on a deploy preview, only on prod or localhost.
The Sunday card change must not widen beyond pastor_leader; weekly-review-for-all was explicitly rejected.
Every new string needs en/es/pt/id or t() renders the raw key on screen, and translated content is drafted then approved before ship.
